title: The model on the table
bodyMd:
A fictional architecture class built a white cardboard model of a proposed library. At review, one visitor praised its clarity while another complained that it looked cold. The tutor asked what the model had been made to test. The students explained that it represented the arrangement of volumes and the relation of entrances to streets; they had not yet selected materials or interior finishes.

The tutor argued that the model was useful within those limits. Its lack of colour simplified the spatial relationships, but it could not justify conclusions about the warmth of the eventual interior. A representation necessarily selects information. The problem is not selection itself, but allowing viewers to mistake an omission for a design decision. The students therefore added a note identifying which features were developed and which remained unresolved.
